title: Reliability collab field lab notes — SLO activation runway
body:
Purpose:
This is a working field-lab brief for running short, measurable experiments that accelerate SLO operationalization across product, serving runtime, and SRE. The goal is a repeatable runway: hypothesis -> small controlled experiment -> telemetry validation -> rollout recipe + runbook.

Background / motivation:
We have a backlog of SLO adoption requests from product teams and several unresolved reliability knobs (batching windows, KV-cache eviction, fallback routing) that interact in non-linear ways with latency and cost. This field lab is designed to let cross-functional pairs test realistic changes against production-like traffic slices, gather signal, and produce a minimal rollout package (SLO definition, alert thresholds, rollback criteria, and playbook).

Scope (what this doc covers):
- Focus on text-generation endpoints and embedding pipelines for initial pilots.
- Surface-level changes (config/traffic routing/batching/quantization profile) only; no model architecture changes here.
- We will run up to three 2-week experiments in parallel for separate risk tiers.

Key hypotheses to test (examples):
1) Moderate KV-cache lifetime increase (x1.5) reduces token cost by 12–18% without increasing p95 latency beyond 5% for seeded conversational workloads.
2) Shorter batching window (reduce from 50ms to 30ms) improves p95 latency for low-concurrency interactive flows at <3% throughput loss.
3) Canary fallback to smaller model variant under high queueing reduces error-budget burn rate by >40% while keeping quality regression within acceptable bounds for internal eval sets.

Experiments (field-lab ledger):
- Experiment A (KV-cache lifetime tweak) — Sprint 1 (2026-02-01 -> 2026-02-14):
  - Setup: instrument prefix-hit metrics + per-request cost attribution. Add AB routing for 10% of production traffic for non-critical teams.
  - Signals to capture: cache-hit ratio by endpoint, per-token cost, p50/p95/p99 latency, error-rate on token generation (timeouts/retries).
  - Roll criteria: if p95 increases by >7% or token error-rate increases by >0.5%, rollback.
  - Owner: Liam Chen (platform infra).

- Experiment B (Batching window tuning) — Sprint 1 & 2:
  - Setup: synthetic low-concurrency traffic + 5% live canary. Measure throughput degradation and latency tail.
  - Signals: queue length distribution, batching aggregation efficiency, latency quantiles, CPU/GPU utilization.
  - Success metric: p95 reduction for interactive flows >=10ms while throughput loss <2%.
  - Owner: Sana Rao (serving runtime).

- Experiment C (Fallback routing policy + small-model canary) — Sprint 2:
  - Setup: implement policy to route to quantized variant when queue delay > threshold. Controlled rollout starting at 5% traffic for internal customers.
  - Signals: user-facing quality regression measured on canary eval set, error-budget burn, customer support tickets.
  - Owner: Oliver Kim (product-hosted-api).

Telemetry & signal plan:
- Primary signals: p50/p95/p99 latency, request success rate, per-token cost, cache-hit ratio, queue wait time, model output quality scores (eval harness), and error-budget burn-rate.
- Observability integration: dashboards per-experiment + anomaly alerts on sudden metric divergence. Instrument sampling for model-eval checks (store 1-in-100 generations).
- Tagging: all traces/metrics from experiments must include lab-experiment-id and experiment-owner.

Success criteria and gating:
- Primary: stable p95 latency within defined guardrails and reduction in expected unit cost or error-budget improvement.
- Secondary: quality drift below defined tolerance across eval prompts (<2% measured metric drop) and no uptick in customer-reported regressions for pilot customers.
- Gate for rollout: documented rollout playbook, runbook with rollback instructions, post-mortem template, and stakeholder signoff.

Stakeholders & roles:
- Experiment owners (listed above) — run the experiment, monitor signals, declare result.
- SRE liaison: Noah Rivera — ensure on-call readiness and incident escalation path.
- Product sponsor: Ava Martinez — approves canary exposure and customer lists.
- Data/telemetry: Matt (Data Platform) — provide aggregated cost and quality dashboards (contact via internal slack #data-ops).
- Legal/compliance review: required for pilots involving customer data in Private deployments.

Sprint cadence & runbook:
- Two-week sprints. Week 0: setup + baseline collection. Week 1: 10–20% canary + monitoring. End of Week 2: decision review (promote/iterate/rollback).
- Daily stand: 15 minutes sync Mon/Wed/Fri during active canaries.
- Decision rubric: green (promote to 50% then staged rollout), amber (iterate with narrower scope), red (rollback).

Dependencies:
- Telemetry plumbing for per-token cost attribution (JIRA-RED-2183).
- Small-model quantized variant build and validation (PR linked in artifacts).
- Access to canary customer groups and gating feature flags (product infra).

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Quality regressions not detected by automated evals -> Mitigation: pair eval with small manual review panel and increase sample rate for a short window.
- Risk: Unexpected error-budget burns -> Mitigation: automated cutoff threshold and rapid rollback runbook with pre-warmed fallback.
- Risk: Cross-team communication gaps -> Mitigation: daily sync + experiment status card in the platform slack channel and page updates.

Communication & documentation:
- Live experiment summary card (Slack): owner posts at start, mid-carry, close.
- Confluence artifact: each experiment gets a single page with hypothesis, results, and final recommendation. Link back to Field Lab Index.

Next steps & immediate action items (owner):
- [PRIORITY] Telemetry work: complete per-token cost aggregation by 2026-02-05 (Owner: Liam Chen, JIRA-RED-2183).
- Prepare quantized model canary build and smoke tests by 2026-02-10 (Owner: Sana Rao, linked PR).
- Identify pilot customers and obtain PM sponsor approvals by 2026-02-12 (Owner: Ava Martinez).
- Schedule 3 rapid tabletop drills with SRE to validate rollback path (Owner: Noah Rivera).

Open questions / discussion points:
- Should canary eval metric thresholds be global or endpoint-specific? Tradeoffs noted: global is simpler; endpoint-specific reduces false positives but adds operational overhead.
- How to account for cold-start variability in tail-latency SLOs vs steady-state? Proposal: baseline windows during low-traffic segments and separate warm/cold SLO variants.

Appendix (quick notes):
- Sample alert thresholds: p95 increase >7% OR error-rate delta >0.5% -> auto-notify escalation channel.
- Suggested dashboard tiles: per-experiment cost delta, cache-hit delta, latency tail split by model-variant, quality metric trend.

This document is intentionally informal — it's a working ledger to be iterated. Final experiments will be published to Confluence with structured templates and archived under the Field Lab Index.
